achan.title: Achan
achan.note: He kept back plunder from Jericho, a Babylonian garment and silver and gold, when all of it was under the ban. Israel lost the next fight because of it.

achor.title: Achor
achor.note: A valley near Jericho, on the border between Judah and Benjamin, named for the trouble Achan brought on Israel.

adam-2.title: Adam
adam-2.note: Not the first man but a place that carries his name. It is named in a single verse of Joshua and nowhere else.

adonizedec.title: Adonizedec
adonizedec.note: The Amorite king of Jerusalem in Joshua's day. When Gibeon made peace with Israel he pulled together five Canaanite kings to attack it, and Joshua marched out to defend the city.

ai.title: Ai
ai.note: A fortified Canaanite city near Bethel. Israel's first attack was thrown back because of Achan's hidden sin, and once that was dealt with Joshua took the city by ambush. The site is usually identified with et-Tell, though digging there has turned up little from the right period.

aijalon.title: Aijalon
aijalon.note: In the valley of Aijalon Joshua told the moon to stand still alongside the sun during the battle against the Amorite coalition. Later it marked the boundary of Danite and Benjamite territory.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

ashtaroth.title: Ashtaroth
ashtaroth.note: Ashtaroth under another spelling, the fortified capital of Og, king of Bashan, east of the Jordan. It went to the half-tribe of Manasseh and then to the Levites of Gershon. The name comes from the goddess Ashtoreth, and the site is generally put at Tell Ashtarah in the Golan.

azekah.title: Azekah
azekah.note: A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

beeroth.title: Beeroth
beeroth.note: It was one of four Hivite cities, with Gibeon, Chephirah and Kiriath-jearim. Their people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by dressing up as travellers from far away. Later it was allotted to Benjamin.

beth-aven.title: Beth-aven
beth-aven.note: House of vanity. It lay in the hill country of Benjamin near Ai and Bethel, served as a boundary marker in Joshua, and was where Israel's forces gathered before Jonathan's fight with the Philistines in 1 Samuel 14.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-horon.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon.note: Twin towns on the pass from the coastal plain up into the hill country. Joshua's army came this way chasing the Canaanite coalition in the battle where the sun stood still.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

carmi-2.title: Carmi
carmi-2.note: Achan's father. Achan took plunder from Jericho that was devoted to God, and Israel lost its next battle because of it.

chephirah.title: Chephirah
chephirah.note: With Gibeon, Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim, one of the four Hivite towns whose people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by posing as travellers from a far country.

debir.title: Debir
debir.note: Othniel took this town in Judah's hill country and won Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife for it. Debir is also the name of a Canaanite king Joshua defeated.

debir-2.title: Debir
debir-2.note: Joshua names him once, and he is a king from the years before the monarchy.

ebal.title: Ebal
ebal.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ebal.note: The mountain of the curses, opposite Mount Gerizim near Shechem. Moses ordered six tribes onto Ebal to speak the covenant's curses while six on Gerizim spoke its blessings, and Joshua built an altar there and wrote the law on stones. A Horite chief descended from Seir carried the name too.

eglon.title: Eglon
eglon.note: A royal Canaanite city in the Shephelah. Its king joined the five Amorite kings Joshua crushed at Gibeon, and the city was destroyed and given to Judah.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gazer.title: Gazer
gazer.note: The same city as Gezer. Pharaoh took it and gave it to his daughter when she married Solomon, and Solomon fortified it along with Hazor and Megiddo. The Gezer Calendar, a little tablet of farming seasons in early Hebrew script, was found there.

gerizim.title: Gerizim
gerizim.note: Opposite Mount Ebal, near Shechem. Six tribes stood on Gerizim to speak the blessings while six on Ebal spoke the curses, as Moses had ordered and Joshua carried out. The Samaritans later built a temple on top as a rival to Jerusalem, which is what the Samaritan woman is asking Jesus about in John 4:20.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gilgal.title: Gilgal
gilgal.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.

girgashite.title: Girgashite
girgashite.note: Descended from Canaan in Genesis 10, and one of the peoples on the list Israel was to drive out. Where exactly they lived is unclear, though they are generally placed in the central hill country.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

goshen-2.title: Goshen
goshen-2.note: Not the Goshen in Egypt but a stretch of Canaan's south that Joshua took, along with a town of the same name in the hill country.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

heshbon.title: Heshbon
heshbon.note: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

hoham.title: Hoham
hoham.note: King of Hebron, and an Amorite. He joined four other kings to besiege Gibeon for making peace with Israel, which brought Joshua on a forced march, and afterwards he was found hiding with the others in a cave at Makkedah and executed.

horam.title: Horam
horam.note: Gezer's king. He came to help Lachish while Joshua had it under siege, and Joshua wiped out him and his army. Gezer itself stayed Canaanite until Solomon.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

japhia-2.title: Japhia
japhia-2.note: Joshua names him once, and he is a king from the years before the monarchy.

jarmuth.title: Jarmuth
jarmuth.note: Its king joined the march on Gibeon after Gibeon made peace with Israel, and Joshua beat them in the battle where the sun stood still.

jehoshua.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua.about: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
jehoshua.note: Joshua, in the longer spelling. Moses's attendant and successor, and one of two from the generation out of Egypt who lived to enter the land. He took Israel over the Jordan, brought down Jericho and divided the land among the tribes. The name means Yahweh saves, the same name Greek renders Jesus.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kadeshbarnea.title: Kadeshbarnea
kadeshbarnea.note: An oasis in the wilderness of Zin, on Canaan's southern edge, where Israel camped for much of the wandering years. The spies went out from here, and the people's fear at their report got that whole generation sentenced to die in the desert. Later it marked the southern boundary of the land.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

libnah.title: Libnah
libnah.note: A royal Canaanite city near Lachish that Joshua took and gave to the Levites in Judah. It held out against Sennacherib's Assyrians. Hamutal, Josiah's wife and mother of two of Judah's last kings, came from there.

makkedah.title: Makkedah
makkedah.note: Five Amorite kings ran from the battle at Gibeon and hid in a cave near this royal city in the Shephelah. Joshua sealed them in until the fighting was over, then brought them out, killed them, and hung their bodies on trees. Then he took the city.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

non.title: Non
non.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
non.note: Joshua's father, of the tribe of Ephraim, more usually spelled Nun and hardly ever seen outside the phrase "Joshua son of Nun."

og.title: Og
og.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
og.note: King of Bashan and, in Deuteronomy, the last of the Rephaim, with a bed over thirteen feet long. Israel beat him and took his whole kingdom.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

piram.title: Piram
piram.note: King of Jarmuth, one of five Amorite kings who besieged Gibeon. Joshua beat them in the battle where the sun stood still, and the five were found hiding in a cave at Makkedah.

rahab.title: Rahab
rahab.note: A prostitute in Jericho. She hid the two spies Joshua sent ahead, and for that, and for the faith she declared in Israel's God, she and her family were spared when the city fell.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

shebarim.title: Shebarim
shebarim.note: Israel's first attack on Ai failed, and the men ran. They were chased down the slope as far as Shebarim, and the defeat was later traced to Achan's sin.

shinar.title: Shinar
shinar.note: The old name for the land of Babylon. The tower of Babel went up there, and much later it was the heart of Nebuchadnezzar's empire.

shittim.title: Shittim
shittim.note: Israel's last camp before crossing into Canaan, on the plain of Moab across from Jericho. It was there that the men were drawn into idolatry with Moabite women.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

zabdi.title: Zabdi
zabdi.note: Achan's grandfather. When Joshua went looking for who had taken the plunder from Jericho, the lot came down through his household.

zarah.title: Zarah
zarah.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zarah.note: Judah's son by Tamar, Perez's twin. His hand came out first and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on it, and then Perez was born ahead of him.

zarchite.title: Zarchite
zarchite.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zarchite.note: A descendant of Zerah. It shows up in the census lists and the rosters in Chronicles and never attaches to anyone well known.

zarthan.title: Zarthan
zarthan.note: The Jordan's waters piled up near Zarthan when Israel crossed on dry ground. Centuries later Solomon's bronze for the temple was cast in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan. Exactly where in the plain it stood is uncertain.
